# requires: store
#
# The negotiation, exercised. `content` names what a record carries and
# `critical` names what a reader must understand or refuse it -- and until this
# scenario existed nothing had ever put a name in either that an implementation
# did not know. Every name in the format has been understood by every reader
# since the format existed, so the branch that refuses was reachable only by a
# writer that does not exist yet.
#
# `plant` is that writer. It forges the declaration on disk because a conforming
# one cannot: an implementation validates its own declaration on the way out and
# will not write a record it could not read back, which is correct and is
# exactly why its own refusal path had no test.
#
# A is the advisory half. The name is decoration, the record still says
# everything a reader needs, and refusing it would be the old integer version's
# only answer to any addition at all. It is read, and the name is carried in
# memory and not written back, because `content` is derived from the data on
# every write and this reader has no data for it.
#
# B is the critical half, and the answer must be the opposite. The distinction
# is not cosmetic: `invalid` says the record is broken and a caller may discard
# it, `unknown-model` says the record is fine and this reader is too old to
# touch it. Go answered `refused` and the other two answered `invalid` for as
# long as the mechanism existed.
#
# Steps 7 and 8 are the consequence. A record a reader must refuse is a record
# it must not claim and must not write an intent onto, and step 9 is the one
# that matters most: a sweep that offered B to an adopter would hand it work it
# has just declared itself unable to understand.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=file
submit B size=64 digest=good src=file
plant A content abstraction.test/hovercraft@7
state A
plant B critical abstraction.test/hovercraft@7
state B
claim B alpha 5000
intent B cancel
orphans

# expect 4: ok [JOB-D1]
# expect 4: state=pending
# expect 5: unknown-model [JOB-D1]
# expect 6: unknown-model [JOB-D7]
# expect 7: unknown-model
# expect 8: unknown-model
# expect 9: ok A
